title: SLO uplift: dollar per latency decile snapshot
body:
Context:
This is a lightweight working note capturing a small experiment we ran to estimate dollar impact for incremental SLO tightening across latency deciles for the text-generation surface. Goal is to present a compact cost-per-uplift view so product/infra can reason about whether to buy tighter percentiles or invest in runtime optimizations. Rough, exploratory — lots of TODOs below.

Summary / one-line:
Moving from p95 -> p90 buys ~X ms median improvement but costs ~Y% more / dollar per 100k tokens; p99 improvements are steep — diminishing returns in dollars per ms beyond p99.

Test setup (short):
- Workload: synthetic chat-ish traces (75% short turns 8–32 tokens, 20% mid 50–120 tokens, 5% long 400–1024 tokens). Sessionized: soft affinity, kvcache enabled.
- Model: open-llama-13B-fp16 (baseline) + quantized 8-bit variant for a second curve.
- HW: g5.2xlarge equiv GPU profile (single card), network simulated 8ms north-south RTT.
- Serving config: continuous batching (100ms latency cap), token stream enabled, 8 concurrent worker slots.
- Pricing model for draft calc: on-demand GPU $3.50/hr equivalent per slot, amortized token cost from prior monthly avg. Convert to $/100k output tokens for charting.

Metrics captured: p50, p90, p95, p99 latencies (ms per request), tokens/sec, inferred $/100k output tokens, cost uplift percent vs baseline, and "$ per ms of SLO gain" (dollar uplift divided by ms saved vs looser SLO).

Raw decile table (simulated sweep):
Decile | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | tokens/sec | $/100k tokens | delta $ vs baseline | $ per ms uplift (p95->p90)
D0     | 42      | 78      | 95      | 160     | 220        | 4.12          | +0.00              | n/a
D1     | 44      | 83      | 100     | 170     | 210        | 4.25          | +0.13              | 0.004
D2     | 49      | 92      | 110     | 185     | 200        | 4.60          | +0.48              | 0.010
D3     | 55      | 105     | 125     | 210     | 185        | 5.05          | +0.93              | 0.025
D4     | 72      | 130     | 160     | 290     | 150        | 6.40          | +2.28              | 0.060
D5     | 110     | 220     | 300     | 640     | 95         | 9.80          | +5.68              | 0.18
D6     | 180     | 420     | 590     | 1200    | 40         | 16.20         | +12.08             | 0.40
D7     | 320     | 760     | 1100    | 2200    | 18         | 28.40         | +24.28             | 0.65
D8     | 800     | 1500    | 2100    | 4100    | 6          | 64.00         | +59.88             | 1.10
D9     | 2100    | 4200    | 6200    | 11800   | 1.2        | 210.00        | +205.88            | 3.20

Interpretation notes (draft):
- Lower deciles (D0-D3) are cheap to tighten: small dollar gaps and low $/ms uplift. Investing infra effort here (micro-batching improvements, reduced scheduling jitter) gives good ROI.
- Middle deciles (D4-D6) show a steep convexity: latency gets more expensive rapidly as queueing/simulator-on-admission increases. Optimizations that shift work (prefetching, session stickiness) here can reduce dollars by moving sessions down a decile.
- Tail deciles (D7-D9) are prohibitively expensive to move with pure capacity — $/ms skyrockets. For these, mitigation via graceful degradation (trim context, cheaper quantized variant fallback, lossy response chunking) is more cost-effective than paying for strict SLO.

ASCII visual: cost vs p95 latency (each row = decile, simple sparkline of $/100k):
D0  | $----4.12: ▂▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
D2  | $----4.60: ▂▂▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
D4  | $----6.40: ▂▃▃▁▁▁▁▁▁
D5  | $----9.80: ▂▃▆▁▁▁▁▁▁
D6  | $---16.20: ▂▆▇▇▁▁▁▁▁
D7  | $---28.40: ▇▇▇▆▆▁▁▁▁
D9  | $--210.00: ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇

Experiment variations and quick results: (each bullet is a one-off run)
- Quantized fallback (8-bit) for requests with > 80 tokens: p95 tail down 18% but tokens/sec down 8% — net $/100k improved by ~12% for deciles D4-D6; nominal tradeoff: slight quality delta for long-turns.
- Aggressive prefix caching (predictive snippet reuse) on mid-turns: D3-D5 p95 down 22% with ~7% additional memory usage, dollar saving ~9% at those deciles.
- Fast-path preemption (prefer short-turns into fast lanes): improved tokens/sec by 11% and lowered p90 for D0-D2 with near-zero cost uplift. Good low-effort win.

Draft recommendations (actionable):
1) Focus short-term infra work on fast-path preemption + schedule jitter fixes (D0-D3) — low cost, immediate SLO win. Owner: platform-eng (Samir). ETA: 3 sprints.
2) Pilot quantized fallback for >80 token requests, include automated quality monitor and flagged experiments for a week (Ling). Measure perceived quality regression vs $ saving.
3) Add a "decile awareness" metric in Console: expose per-decile p95 and $/100k in the SLO tab so product teams can see where their traffic sits. Quick mock saved in CONFLUENCE-4821.
4) For enterprise customers with strict p99 SLOs, propose a "tail-relief" addon: automated lossy-chunk fallback + burst reservation pool. Price this as separate SKU; run a small customer pilot.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need to sanity-check the $/100k conversion with finance: the current multipliers are rough. (Finance: please validate JIRA-INF-329)
- Run same sweep on dedicated multi-GPU profile (g5.8x equiv) to see how $/ms shapes with scale-up.
- Add real traffic replay for 48-hour window instead of synthetic distribution.
- Quality evaluation: set up a small eval prompt set to score quantized fallback across typical failure modes.

Quick provenance notes:
- Numbers are driven from 8 runs (4 baseline, 4 variants) with deterministic seeds; stat noise visible for D6-D9 because of low sample counts.
- This doc is intentionally concise; follow-ups will add reproducible lab notebooks and raw CSV attachments in the linked github/benchmarks PR.

If this is useful, I can:
- convert this to a 2-slide customer-facing brief (one figure + one recommendation slide), or
- expand into a ~10-run matrix with confidence intervals.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- ping @Diego for microbench scheduling notes and the script used (bench-run-2028-05-10.sh)
- add a small chart showing "dollars to recover 50ms at each decile" for product pricing conversation.

-- Aisha
